Maya: Heads-up — microbench on a100-prod-2 after today's driver bump (545.23) shows a kernel mispick for sequence-length 128 workloads. The runtime picked 'matmul-large-block-fp32' instead of the tensor-core bf16 path, p95 latency up ~15%. I dumped the probe + autotune hints below.

Raj: Can you paste the probe log and the microbench numbers? Curious if it's an SM detection issue or a heuristic change.

Maya: Sure, log excerpt and perf numbers:
```
PROBE: gpu_id=0000:3b:00.0 sm=80 pci=0x1e86 driver=545.23
AUTOTUNE: seqlen=32 -> kernel=tc_bf16_opt average=1.9ms
AUTOTUNE: seqlen=128 -> kernel=matmul-large-block average=6.2ms
AUTOTUNE: seqlen=512 -> kernel=kv-prefetch-matmul average=18.1ms
MICROBENCH: workload=chatty-128 tokens/single-stream
   before-driver: p50=4.7ms p95=9.1ms
   after-driver:  p50=5.1ms p95=10.4ms (15% p95 regression)
KV-LOG: kv_cache_hits=87% kv_evictions=0.6%
HINTS: detected_tensorcore=true bf16_supported=true fp8_supported=false
```

Lin: Interesting. The probe shows tensor cores reported available, but runtime still selected fp32 kernel at seqlen=128. Two hypotheses: (1) the driver changed the performance curve for the tc_bf16 kernel (e.g., launched threadblock sizing), or (2) our kernel selection heuristic relies on a microbench metric that regressed due to driver-level FP16 math changes.

Sara: Also check for subtle FP16 denorm/rounding mode differences. We had a similar flake when a driver changed fp16 accumulation semantics and made our bf16 kernels slower on certain SM configs.

Raj: Quick experiment: run the microprobe that times a tiny GEMM shape we use as a tensor-core litmus: 128x64x64 bf16 mul-add repeated 1000x. If the TC kernel now has worse latency than the fallback, mark it as "soft-disabled" in the per-GPU autotune db.

Maya: Ran that probe on a100-prod-2:
```
GEMM-LITMUS: shape=128x64x64 dtype=bf16 runs=1000
   tc_bf16_opt avg=2.7ms std=0.12ms
   matmul-large-block avg=2.1ms std=0.08ms
```
So TC path is actually slower on this build. That explains the pick. But weird because earlier driver had tc faster.

Lin: If the microprobe flips, we should record a timestamped capability flag in the node metadata: e.g., gpu.features.tensorcore_violated=true with a reason string referencing the probe id. That lets the planner avoid TC kernels without losing the model-level hint that the HW nominally supports it.

Raj: Agree. Also let's gate kernel picks by sequence-length distribution threshold rather than single seqlen boundary. For example: if >30% of requests are seqlen>=128 AND the microprobe shows TC slower for the 128 workload, prefer matmul-large-block for that node. This avoids per-request oscillation and KV thrash.

Maya: Noted another effect: under mixed traffic (32/128/512) the KV cache usage pattern produced uneven strides and we saw small evictions (kv_evictions to 1.8%) when using the tc path for 128. Switching to matmul-large-block reduced evictions and improved overall tail. So kernel pick affects KV locality.

Sara: That's classic cross-layer coupling — kernel choice changes memory access shape which interacts with kv cache stride. We should add a lightweight kv_thrash_probe as part of autotune: run representative prefix sequences and measure kv_eviction_rate.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: runtime/autotune/2026-03-18T14:30Z -> cluster=a100-canary-1 with config=autotune.seqlen_split=128 (canary-duration=2h)

ops-bot: Ops note — if we detect p95 regression >10% on canary, automatic rollback to previous autotune snapshot will trigger. Also we can pin driver 543.10 on the fleet if needed.

Lin: Implementation plan: (1) add microprobe for gemm litmus + kv_thrash probe (2) store probe result as node capability flags with reason and probe_ts (3) update kernel selector to consult node capabilities and sequence-distribution histograms (4) rollout canary which prefers the fallback kernel when kv_eviction_rate > 1% or tc_litmus slower.

Raj: I'll take (1) and (2), Maya can drive (3) and (4) with me. Sara can add the eval checks to quality-metrics so we don't miss regressions.

Maya: Sounds good. I'll add a temporary flag arch.autotune.soft_disable_tensorcore=true for canary to force the fallback without changing heuristics globally. After 2h canary we'll flip based on metrics.

Raj: One more ask — capture the raw kernel timings and launch params (block dims, shared mem) in the probe log so we can file a driver bug if launch config changed under driver 545.23.

Maya: Will do, pushing probe artifacts to s3://redwood-testing/autotune/probes/2450004321/ now. Link: https://s3.redwood-internal/autotune/probes/2450004321

Lin: :thumbsup:

Sara: :+1: please add a short blurb to the release notes about the canary and the probe approach so SRE/customer support know why kernel picks changed.

Maya: Will add release note and a small dashboard tile under runtime->autotune->canary-2450004321.

Raj: Thanks everyone — let's sync in the 10min on-call slot after canary starts to decide final roll.

ops-bot: acknowledged. monitoring alerts will post in #incidents if thresholds breach.
